english.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice before an adjective for “fairly,” “quite,” or “pretty,” sometimes with deliberate understatement.
Use this as the all-purpose everyday adverb for a moderate degree, as in “quite wet.”
This is the all-purpose choice for saying that something is quite or somewhat so, as in 幾乾.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying something is fairly or quite so, without suggesting an extreme.
Use this for the ‘fairly’ or ‘quite’ sense when no specific comparison is being made.
Use this before an adjective when “rather” means fairly or quite, as in “rather good.”
